units.text: What is the meaning of: “In Paradise there is a gate called Ar-Rayyan”?

The questioner in this question says: What is narrated in the hadith: “In Paradise there is a gate called Ar-Rayyan; none shall enter it except those who fast.” Does this mean: are the fasting people meant those who fast only the month of Ramadan, or those who fast voluntary fasts such as Mondays and Thursdays and the white days? Benefit us, may you be rewarded.

What is meant by that: those who fast the obligatory fast, those who maintain the obligatory fast, Ramadan, and likewise what Allah has obligated upon them of fasting for expiations and vows. These have a gate; the gate of Ar-Rayyan, they enter through it. When they have entered, it is closed.

And if they have other deeds, they will be called from many gates, but they enter from this gate, the gate of fasting. The believer who establishes prayer, pays zakah (obligatory almsgiving), fasts Ramadan, and is mindful of Allah; he will be called from all the gates, but this gate none enters with them except those who fast, those who maintained the performance of the obligatory fast. Yes.
Presenter: May Allah reward you well.
